subject: Residual covariance matrix not positive definite in Mplus but not in lavaan

messages.author: ccaed8d972a5ce78
messages.subject: Residual covariance matrix not positive definite in Mplus but not in lavaan
parts:
Hi

I'm testing for longitudinal measurement invariance using CFA (3 time points, 3 factors, 19 ordinal items). I have run my configural model in both lavaan and Mplus. Both sets of results provide warnings about high correlations between the same items across time (some of my items show very little change), but only Mplus provides a warning saying the "residual covariance matrix is not positive definite". 

Is there any reason that lavaan wouldn't have provided that warning? My understanding is that lavaan would provide that warning is the matrix was positive. I think that the models are specified identically in Mplus and R, and the model fit and parameter estimates are basically the same - is there something I might have done to cause the warning to show up in Mplus and not in lavaan. 

Next step will be to figure out what to do if the matrix is positive definite (so any suggestions on that note would be great), but I wanted to resolve this problem first.

I'm new to R and lavaan so I might have missed something obvious but I have looked around quite a lot and haven't been able to figure it out. Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks 
Simon

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Residual covariance matrix not positive definite in Mplus but not in lavaan
parts:
Start by looking at the matrix itself. If this is an observed variable residual matrix, and if those observed variables have no free or nonzero residual covariances specified, then the residual covariance matrix is diagonal, with residual variances on the diagonal and 0 elsewhere.
     If the matrices are substantially different, then my first suspect is a syntax error--syntax error and data handling error are the most likely suspects in any "unexpected" SEM result, unfortunately.
